newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo customs accuse tobacco makers of smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Yugo customs accuse tobacco makers of smuggling.

text.p: The head of the Yugoslav customs accused the domestic tobacco industry of aiding cigarette smuggling and announced a crackdown on the illicit trade, Belgrade papers reported on Friday.

"Federal Customs Administration has reliable information that the domestic tobacco industry is considerably helping illegal cigarette trade," Mihalj Kertes, director of the Yugoslav Customs Administration, was quoted by Nasa Borba daily as saying.
Kertes said the local tobacco producers were making substantial financial gains through smuggling and avoiding customs duties.

He was responding to earlier complaints by Yugoslavia's tobacco industry that the government was not doing enough to clamp down on the booming illegal cigarette trade which was threatening to close their factories.
They warned the industry sold only 202 tonnes of home produced cigarettes in March or 10 percent of the total monthly consumption estimated at around 2,000 tonnes.

Kertes particularly charged the management of the country's largest tobacco producer Duvanska Industrija Nis (DIN) of taking the lead in slandering the customs administration to cover up its illegal activities.
In 1996, DIN had fictitiously exported 4,994 tonnes of cigarettes (about 520 truckloads) to the value of 260 million dinars ($53.6 million) mostly to Croatia's Eastern Slavonian region, he said.

The federal customs has reliable information that those cigarettes did not pass customs in Eastern Slavonia and that they were exported to non-existent firms or companies whose owners reside in Yugoslavia, Kertes said.

In the first quarter of 1997 DIN exported 1,997 tonnes of cigarettes to the value of 104 million dinars, of which 1,671 tonnes were exported to Eastern Slavonia and 126 tonnes to the Bosnian Serb republic, he said.
These cigarettes were not reported to customs of Eastern Slavonia and re-entered Yugoslavia through illegal channels.
Kertes said his administration together with the police would launch a fight against all forms of illegal imports, especially against all war and other profiteers.

Within one month the federal government will pass a regulation introducing compulsory tax stamps on all imported goods subject to customs and excise duties, he added. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 43 05 ($ = 4.85 Yugoslav Dinars)
